proposer.mechanism: Block-Aggression Gate: replace base AFG's 'sum of signed contracts >= flow_threshold' criterion with a single-print dominance test. Maintain a deque of (ts_event_ns, aggressor_side, size) over the trailing 10s. Skip BUY when ANY single SELL-aggressor print in the window has size >= block_size (default 3 contracts) AND net signed flow is adverse (net_flow < 0). Mirror for SELL. Reduce-only always submits. After a skip, _position_flat=True (identical anti-cascade to base AFG). Subscribe to trade ticks; prune by ts_event <= order.ts_init.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG aggregates over many small prints. A large single adverse aggressor print is hypothesized to be more informative about regime (institutional / sweep activity is well-known in microstructure as a short-term drift predictor) than the same net volume distributed across many small noise prints. AFG currently fires on small noise as long as the cumulative signed sum exceeds 2.0, missing the distinction.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission, zero slippage cost model (verified). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG: $1255.50. Both prior pc runs underperformed base AFG (r1 burst-gate: $487; r2 persistent-chain: $1093). A block-aggression gate targets a qualitatively different signal axis (single-print dominance) than either prior attempt.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) -- replaces cumulative threshold with single-print dominance test. Also informed by afg-pc-r1 (acceleration failed) and afg-pc-r2 (chain failed).
proposer.alternatives_considered: (a) Order-routing aggressiveness changes -- skipped as out of scope. (b) Lower flow_threshold -- considered but is pure parameter tuning. (c) Dual-window confirmation (3s AND 10s both adverse) -- considered as a precision-tightener but inherits r1's structural problem of skipping less than AFG.

objections.text: MES typical trade sizes are 1-5 contracts; a 3-contract print is not a 'block'. The mechanism's identification of institutional vs retail flow is dubious at this size scale -- the block_size threshold may pick up almost all moderately-active periods, making the gate behave similarly to AFG's level gate but at lower skip rate. The 'block aggression' hypothesis lacks empirical grounding for MES at this scale.

Clearly superior untried alternative: LOWER base AFG's flow_threshold from 2.0 to 1.0 (or similar). Both prior pc runs (r1 burst, r2 chain) attempted orthogonal/structural changes and underperformed AFG's level gate. Base AFG NOTES show broad-based wins (10/12 dates) with the existing precision-positive level signal -- the natural extension is MORE of the same (more skips at lower magnitudes), not a qualitatively different signal. Block-aggression gate has not been tried but neither has the simpler 'lower threshold' refinement, which more directly aligns with AFG's empirical strength.

Block-aggression gate as proposed will produce STRICTLY FEWER skips than base AFG (a single dominant print is a much rarer event than a cumulative >=2.0 imbalance). r1's burst-only gate failed precisely because it skipped fewer trades than AFG (~7% vs 21.6%). The proposed mechanism inherits this structural risk.
block_size=3 is an arbitrary default with no microstructure-literature anchor for MES at this cadence.

suggested_alternatives: Lower base AFG flow_threshold from 2.0 to ~1.0 -- direct extension of AFG's empirical strength (precision-positive level skips). Pair with a thin-market noise floor (e.g., min trade prints in window) to prevent misfires.
Dual-window confirmation (3s AND 10s both adverse and >= respective thresholds) -- tightens precision but has fewer-skips risk.
criticizer.reasoning: Block-aggression gate at MES contract sizes lacks empirical grounding and structurally inherits the 'fewer skips' failure mode of r1. A cleaner untried direction -- lower the existing threshold -- aligns with AFG's broad empirical strength and was not considered.

proposer.mechanism: Dual-Window AFG: identical to base AFG (signed-flow deque, reduce-only submit, _position_flat anti-cascade) EXCEPT compute net_flow over TWO trailing windows simultaneously -- short (3s) and long (10s). Skip BUY when BOTH (a) net_flow_short <= -short_threshold (default 1.0) AND (b) net_flow_long <= -long_threshold (default 2.0, identical to base AFG). Mirror for SELL. Reduce-only always submits; _position_flat=True after skip. This is a level-AND-level intersection: skip only when adverse pressure is BOTH currently active (3s) AND sustained (10s).
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG fires when cumulative 10s flow exceeds threshold regardless of recency. A 10s-old burst of selling can dominate net_flow_long even after the immediate market has cleared. Dual-window confirmation eliminates these stale-signal skips: the 3s requirement ensures the adverse pressure is still active at decision time. Higher precision per skip; fewer false-positive skips where the market has already absorbed the prior burst.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero costs. Base AFG: $1255.50. Dual-window intersection produces FEWER but HIGHER-PRECISION skips than AFG. If the precision gain (better per-skip P&L avoidance) exceeds the recall loss (fewer total adverse moments caught), realized_pnl improves.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) -- preserves the signed-flow primitive, threshold structure, anti-cascade semantics. Replaces single-window threshold with dual-window AND-intersection. Distinct from r1 (which used a ratio/acceleration test, not level-AND-level).
proposer.alternatives_considered: (a) Block-aggression gate (round 1, rejected: lacks empirical grounding at MES scale). (b) Lower flow_threshold -- considered but pure parameter tuning; dual-window adds structural justification (recency confirmation). (c) Hybrid lower-threshold AND dual-window -- rejected as too many simultaneous changes for one test. (d) Asymmetric short/long windows (e.g., 2s/8s) -- defaulted to 3s/10s for direct comparability with base AFG.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 objections addressed: (A) MAJOR 'block-aggression lacks MES grounding' -- abandoned mechanism entirely. (B) MAJOR 'lower-threshold is superior alternative' -- partially adopted (short_threshold=1.0 is a lower threshold for the short window) but structurally embedded in a dual-window framework. (C) MAJOR 'fewer-skips structural risk' -- acknowledged; the dual-window is INTENTIONALLY a precision-tightener, betting that AFG's stale-signal skips are net-negative even though its overall skip set is +704% vs simple.

objections.text: Same fewer-skips structural risk r1 fell into. Dual-window intersection mechanically produces a strict SUBSET of AFG's skip set (every skip requires AFG's gate to also fire on the long window). r1's burst gate already empirically demonstrated that subsetting AFG's skips underperforms (-$767 vs AFG). The 'stale signal' hypothesis is plausible but the asymmetric empirical evidence -- AFG wins on 10/12 dates broadly -- suggests stale-signal skips are NOT a dominant source of error in AFG. Without independent evidence that AFG's 10s window contains a meaningful fraction of stale-burst skips, this is a precision-tightening bet against the existing empirical pattern.

Clearly superior untried alternative still: simply LOWER the existing 10s threshold from 2.0 to 1.0 without adding a second window. The dual-window structure dilutes the parameter test by combining the threshold change with a structural change; if the algo fails, we cannot distinguish whether (a) lowering threshold was wrong, or (b) the dual-window structure was wrong. A clean single-knob test (just threshold=1.0) with a thin-market noise floor (require >= 3 prints in the window) is the more informative experiment.

3s/10s window pair is the same as r1's window pair, raising the risk of empirical collinearity between this algo's skip set and r1's skip set; if r1 underperformed because 3s windows are too noisy at MES cadence, this algo inherits that noise.

suggested_alternatives: Clean threshold-lowering test: base AFG with flow_threshold=1.0 (down from 2.0), guarded by a thin-market floor (e.g., min_prints=3 in the 10s window). Single-knob change, directly tests 'AFG's residual edge is in more skips at lower magnitudes.'
criticizer.reasoning: Dual-window intersection inherits r1's fewer-skips failure mode and dilutes the cleaner parameter-test that directly extends AFG's empirical strength. The threshold-lowering test (with a thin-market floor to avoid 1-contract noise misfires) is the more informative untried direction.

proposer.mechanism: Threshold-Lowered AFG with thin-market floor: identical to base AFG (single 10s rolling window of signed aggressor flow over a deque pruned by ts_event; reduce-only always submits; _position_flat=True after skip) EXCEPT (a) flow_threshold lowered from 2.0 to 1.0 (skip BUY when net_flow <= -1.0; skip SELL when net_flow >= +1.0); (b) thin-market noise floor: the gate requires at least min_prints=3 trade prints in the 10s window before it can fire (if len(deque) < min_prints, do NOT skip -- submit unconditionally, identical to AFG's warm-up behavior). All other AFG semantics preserved: trade-tick subscription, look-ahead-free pruning, reduce-only short-circuit.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG's flow_threshold=2.0 implicitly treats every 1- or 2-contract net adverse imbalance as below the signal-to-noise threshold. But base AFG's empirical evidence (broad 10/12 date wins, +704.8% vs simple) shows its existing skip set is high-precision -- the marginal value of adding skips at lower magnitudes should be positive as long as we filter out trivial-trade-count noise. The thin-market floor (min_prints=3) prevents the lower threshold from firing on near-empty windows where a single small print would gate.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero commission, zero slippage cost model (verified). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG: realized_pnl=$1255.50, +704.8% vs simple. Lowering threshold to 1.0 expects skip rate to rise from 21.6% to ~25-30%. If the additional skips are structurally homogeneous with AFG's existing skips (same level criterion, just lower magnitude), they should be similarly precision-positive. Falsifiable prediction: realized_pnl on the 12-day train window will exceed base AFG's $1255.50 by at least 5% (PASS margin). Failure modes: (a) if 1-contract net imbalances are dominantly noise rather than signal even after the min_prints floor, additional skips lose more than they save -- hypothesis falsified; (b) if the threshold drop produces meaningfully more skips on the 2 losing dates (20260308, 20260311) without hurting the 10 winning dates, the algo passes.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) -- preserves every mechanic except (a) lowered threshold (2.0 -> 1.0) and (b) added min_prints=3 thin-market floor. Distinct from afg-pc-r1 (which used burst-ratio acceleration) and afg-pc-r2 (which used persistent-chain skipping). This is a pure single-knob refinement of AFG's existing precision-positive level criterion in the direction the empirical evidence supports.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (a) Block-aggression gate (round 1, rejected: not empirically grounded at MES sizes). (b) Dual-window confirmation (round 2, rejected: structural tightener, inherits r1's fewer-skips problem). (c) Lower threshold without min_prints floor -- rejected: would misfire in thin windows where a single small aggressor would gate. (d) Threshold=0.5 -- rejected as too aggressive for first attempt; if 1.0 passes, can sweep lower in follow-up. (e) min_prints=5 -- rejected as too restrictive; 3 is a minimal anti-noise guard.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 2 objections fully adopted: (A) MAJOR 'fewer-skips risk in dual-window' -- abandoned dual-window, switched to single-knob threshold lowering which produces MORE skips (the opposite direction); (B) MAJOR 'cleaner threshold-only test' -- adopted verbatim with the suggested min_prints=3 thin-market floor; (C) MINOR '3s window collinearity with r1' -- moot (no 3s window in this proposal).

objections.text: flow_threshold=1.0 vs 0.5 vs 1.5 is parameter risk; 1.0 chosen as a moderate step from base AFG's 2.0. Acceptable as first-attempt default with a falsifiable prediction.
min_prints=3 vs 2 vs 5 is also a parameter choice without literature anchor. Acceptable -- it's a minimal anti-noise guard intended only to prevent pathological 1-trade-window misfires.

criticizer.reasoning: Mechanism is logically coherent (strictly extends AFG's precision-positive skip set in the direction empirical evidence supports), distinct from both prior pc runs, has a principled thin-market guard, and commits to a falsifiable >=5% realized_pnl improvement vs base AFG. No remaining BLOCKING or MAJOR objections; no clearly superior untried alternative within the AFG-refinement family.
